surprises.description: Nucor reported $5.80 per share, slightly below the preview’s $5.85 key bar and the $5.85–$5.95 base case, although it beat the midpoint of its own guidance by about 3.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Earnings of $5.80 per share, beating the guidance midpoint by roughly 3.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 EPS vs. ~$5.85 (not $5.71)” and the base scenario’s “$5.85–5.95.”

surprises.description: Capital spending is expected to come in at or below the original $2.5 billion plan and decline further in 2027, rather than stepping up and pressuring the free-cash-flow outlook. Nucor also reported $1.6 billion of Q3 free cash flow, though the preview gave no specific FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx expected at or slightly below the original $2.5 billion estimate and set to decline further in 2027, boosting free cash flow”; “$1.6 billion of free cash flow in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A 2027 capex preview is a plausible surprise item in either direction” and “a 2027 capex step-up above $2.5B pressures the FCF story.”

surprises.description: Nucor raised its long-term annual EBITDA contribution forecast for Towers and Structures by one-third, from $150 million to about $200 million, citing a backlog that more than doubled year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its long-term annual EBITDA contribution forecast for its Towers and Structures business to ~$200 million (up from $150 million)”; backlog “has more than doubled year-to-date.”

surprises.description: The West Virginia sheet mill remains on its expected ramp schedule, but management said start-up costs will be similar to or higher than in 2026, adding a cost headwind the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elevated start-up costs expected at levels similar to or higher than 2026.”
